tagline: We Open Access to Space to Improve Life on Earth
hero_kpi_rationale: The development of the Neutron launch vehicle is the primary strategic driver of future growth, enabling access to heavy constellation and human spaceflight markets, with significant leverage on revenue and competitive positioning.

kpis.name: Successful Launch Missions
kpis.explanation: Total number of successful orbital launches since 2017.
kpis.description: Since 2017, Rocket Lab has completed 75 successful missions with Electron, solidifying its leadership position in the small launch vehicle market.

kpis.name: Satellites Deployed into Orbit
kpis.explanation: Total number of satellites or payloads launched by Rocket Lab.
kpis.description: Rocket Lab has deployed over 200 spacecraft for government and commercial customers across 75 missions.
kpis.signal: Over 200 satellites deployed, indicating strong customer demand

kpis.name: Total Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Headcount increased from 1,400 in 2022 to over 2,600 by end-2025, reflecting strong operational growth.
kpis.signal: Rapid headcount growth to support expansion

kpis.name: SDA Tranche 3 Contract Value
kpis.explanation: Total potential value of the contract for 18 satellites with the U.S. space agency.
kpis.description: The contract with the Space Development Agency (SDA) for 18 satellites has a potential value of $816 million, with delivery scheduled for 2029.

kpis.name: Neutron Payload Capacity
kpis.explanation: Maximum weight the Neutron launch vehicle will be able to carry to low Earth orbit (reusable configuration).
kpis.description: The Neutron launch vehicle, in reusable configuration, will be capable of carrying up to 13,000 kg to low Earth orbit, significantly expanding the company's service offering.
kpis.signal: 13-ton capacity to LEO, positions RKLB in the medium/heavy segment

kpis.name: Global Launch Frequency Ranking 2025
kpis.explanation: Rocket Lab's position in terms of orbital launch frequency in 2025.
kpis.description: In 2025, Electron was the second most frequently used orbital launch vehicle globally, behind SpaceX Falcon 9.
kpis.signal: Second most used launch vehicle worldwide in 2025

kpis.name: Target Date for First Neutron Launch
kpis.explanation: Target date for the first orbital flight of the Neutron launch vehicle.
kpis.description: The first Neutron launch is now targeted for Q4 2026, following a failure during the first stage tank test in January 2026.
kpis.signal: Launch targeted for Q4 2026 following delay due to test failure

kpis.name: Mynaric Acquisition (Laser Communications)
kpis.explanation: Acquisition of a European leader in space-based laser communications.
kpis.description: The acquisition of Mynaric in April 2026 strengthens Rocket Lab's capabilities in high-speed laser communications between satellites.
kpis.signal: Integration of key space-based optical communication technologies

risks.title: Uncontrolled Growth
risks.score_rationale: The company has experienced rapid growth and must manage its resources to sustain this expansion. The risk is high due to organizational complexity and challenges in scaling operations.

risks.title: Dependence on Government Orders
risks.score_rationale: The company is highly dependent on government contracts, making it vulnerable to policy and funding changes. The risk is high due to the significant proportion of revenue derived from government contracts.

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a fast-evolving market with growing competition. The risk is high due to the need to develop new technologies to remain competitive.

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company is subject to strict government regulations, particularly regarding safety and export controls. The risk is high due to regulatory complexity and the consequences of non-compliance.

risks.title: Dependence on Key Customers
risks.score_rationale: The company relies heavily on a few key customers, making it vulnerable to customer loss. The risk is high due to the significant share of revenue from these customers.

risks.title: New Technology Development Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company must develop new technologies to remain competitive. The risk is high due to the complexity of development processes and the impact of potential failures.

risks.title: Financing Risks
risks.score_rationale: The company has incurred financial losses and must manage its resources to maintain financial stability. The risk is high due to the need to fund ongoing operations and capital investments.

ai_positioning.summary: Rocket Lab does not reference any strategic use of artificial intelligence in its recent communications. The company focuses on space engineering, launch vehicles, satellites, and optical communications, with no mention of AI as a technological or commercial enabler.
evidence: No mention of AI in the Business, MD&A, or Risk sections of the 10-K
No reference to AI algorithms, machine learning, or intelligent automation in operations
Cited innovations are hardware-based: 3D-printed engines, composite structures, booster recovery, laser communications
